newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures cut losses, still lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures cut losses, still lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures cut the biggest early losses incurred after some firmer-than-forecast domestic economic data but remained moderately lower in morning pit trading.

Traders tied the quick drop in June U.S. Treasury bond futures to a larger fall than forecast in weekly jobless claims coupled with a slightly bigger rise in core retail-level inflation than expected.
April U.S. consumer prices rose 0.1 percent and the rate minus food and energy increased 0.3 percent against respectively forecasts for up 0.1 percent and up 0.2 percent.
Weekly U.S. jobless claims fell 31,000 to 319,000 from an upwardly revised 350,000 the prior week and compared to forecasts for down 7,000 at 340,000 from the prior week's original 347,000.

"The claims seem to have come from left field here," said Jim Collins, senior vice president, Smith Barney. But he also noted that claims last week were skewed upward by flooding and have simply returned to the more-typical recent levels.
Other said T-bonds, which surprised some by not rising as much as they had expected Wednesday after tame producer price index, proved relatively well-supported after CPI and claims.
